speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For the last four Budget speeches, I have used two files and taken up slightly over two hours.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This time, the major changes that we have to respond to – economic slowdown, climate change and growing uncertainties – added many pages.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Then, the global climate across the world – psychological, economic – was hit by the sudden storm of a virus outbreak.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, over the past few weeks, my colleagues in Cabinet, in the Ministry of Finance (MOF) have been managing various fronts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To support our national efforts, the Budget file grew and grew.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, today, I have three files instead of two.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is the weakest growth since the 2008 Financial Crisis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Just as the global economy was beginning to recover, the Coronavirus Disease 2019 (COVID-19) outbreak hit us.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The tourism and aviation industries are most directly affected.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Visitor arrivals to Singapore and air traffic through Changi have declined, and with it, hotel occupancy rates.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The virus outbreak has also disrupted supply chains and created ripple effects on other sectors, especially now that our economy is so much more integrated with China's.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, the duration and severity of this outbreak and the impact on the global economy are still unclear.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While MTI's baseline is for GDP growth to come in at 0.5% for the full year, we must be prepared that the economic impact may be worse than we projected.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our immediate concern is to protect you and your families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will put in every effort to slow down the spread of the virus.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The bulk of this will go to the Ministry of Health.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is on top of the substantial resources already committed each year to public health.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: You have exemplified the resilience and indomitable spirit of our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am confident that, together, we will stay strong and get through these trying times.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The first is the Stabilisation and Support Package.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will stabilise the economy and support our workers and enterprises, by helping workers to stay in their jobs and enterprises with cash flow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will give additional help to sectors more directly affected by the outbreak.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Households will be impacted by the slowdown, too.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In every Budget, we always provide support to families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But in view of the current situation, we will have a special Care and Support Package, to provide additional, timely help to more households with cost of living.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, let me elaborate on how we will help our workers and enterprises to weather the near-term economic uncertainties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We want to help our workers retain their jobs, and use any lull period to upgrade their skills, and be ready when the upturn comes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To help our workers stay employed, I will support enterprises by defraying their wage cost, through two schemes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will introduce a Jobs Support Scheme to help enterprises retain their local workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This payment will be given to employers by the end of July this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With over 1.9 million local employees in Singapore, this will cost the Government $1.3 billion and benefit all enterprises and their local employees.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For enterprises that have invested in raising productivity, I urge them to continue to upgrade and to share the gains with their workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Hence, I will enhance the Wage Credit Scheme to support wage increases for Singaporean employees.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Currently, the Wage Credit Scheme co-funds wage increases for Singaporean employees earning a gross monthly wage of up to $4,000.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will raise the monthly wage ceiling from $4,000 to $5,000, for qualifying wage increases given in 2019 and 2020, so that more Singaporean employees will benefit.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will also raise the Government co‑funding levels for 2019 and 2020 qualifying wage increases by five-percentage points, to 20% and 15% respectively.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With these enhancements, another $1.1 billion will go to about 90,000 enterprises, to benefit more than 700,000 Singaporean employees.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Stabilisation and Support Package will also provide economy-wide support to help enterprises with cash flow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, I will grant a Corporate Income Tax Rebate for Year of Assessment 2020, at a rate of 25% of tax payable, capped at $15,000 per company.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This rebate will benefit all tax-paying companies, and cost about $400 million.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will also enhance several tax treatments under the corporate tax system for one year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For instance, I will allow enterprises a faster write-down of their investments in plant and machinery, and renovation and refurbishment, incurred for Year of Assessment 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will put more cash in the hands of our enterprises.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, hotels can now take advantage of this lull period to carry out upgrading work, and be better prepared for the upturn.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With the large part of the risks taken up by the Government, I trust that our financial institutions will do their part to support viable small and medium enterprises (SMEs).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also support tenants and lessees of Government-managed properties, including those under JTC, the Housing and Development Board (HDB), Singapore Land Authority, Singapore Tourism Board and Sentosa Development Corporation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They can approach our agencies to discuss options for more flexible rental payments, such as instalment plans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Each request will be assessed individually, taking into account the enterprise’s circumstances.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To help employers in these sectors retain and reskill workers, we will enhance support under the Adapt and Grow initiative for this year, specifically through redeployment programmes in the tourism, aviation, retail and food services sectors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For these sectors, we will extend the funding period for reskilling from three months to a maximum of six months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These workers can make full use of the downtime for training and upskilling, to prepare for the recovery.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also help affected sectors with their operating costs and cash flow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For the tourism sector, I will grant a Property Tax Rebate of 30% for the year 2020, for the accommodation and function room components of licensed hotels and serviced apartments, and prescribed Meetings, Incentives, Conventions and Exhibitions (MICE) venues.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: International cruise and regional ferry terminals will receive a 15% Property Tax Rebate and the Integrated Resorts will receive a 10% Property Tax Rebate.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will take on 80% of the risk of the loan.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will provide more cash flow on top of the enhanced working capital loan I announced earlier.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For the aviation sector, we will implement a suite of measures, comprising rebates on aircraft landing and parking charges, assistance to ground handling agents, and rental rebates for shops and cargo agents at Changi Airport.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will also grant a 15% Property Tax Rebate for Changi Airport.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To support commercial establishments in the food services and retail business, the Government will take the lead.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The National Environment Agency (NEA) will provide a full month of rental waiver to stallholders in NEA-managed hawker centres and markets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Other Government agencies, like HDB, will provide half a month of rental waiver to its commercial tenants.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To support establishments that operate in private property, I will also grant a 15% Property Tax Rebate for qualifying commercial properties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I strongly urge landlords to pass this on to their tenants by reducing rentals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Ministry of Transport (MOT) has announced a Point-to-Point Support Package.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am heartened to know that many taxi and private hire car operators have come out strongly to support the initiative by matching the Government’s contribution.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This spirit of partnership is what we need to weather this challenging period together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Details of the Stabilisation and Support Package are in the Annex.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Ministers-in-charge of the various measures will share further details in due course.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to monitor the situation closely.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: If needed, we can and are prepared to do more.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will speak about the Care and Support Package for households later in my speech.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The COVID-19 outbreak is a stark reminder of the continued importance of maintaining a sound fiscal footing to deal with surprises and unexpected scenarios.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In particular, we are able to mount a decisive response to support Singaporeans and workers through uncertain times only because of good long-term planning.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I announced in 2018 that we plan to raise the Goods and Services Tax (GST) by two percentage points, to 9%, sometime from 2021 to 2025.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is to raise recurrent revenues to meet our recurrent spending, particularly for healthcare.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In other words, the GST rate will remain at 7% in 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, we will not be able to put off the increase indefinitely.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In fact, this outbreak has reinforced the importance of continued investment in our healthcare system, including the capability to deal with outbreaks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will assess carefully the appropriate time for the increase.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But rest assured we will provide Singaporeans sufficient lead time.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I want to assure everyone that when we raise the GST rate, we will ensure that our taxes and transfers system remain progressive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to absorb GST on publicly-subsidised healthcare and education.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: GST is paid by all in Singapore, including foreigners working and visiting here.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over and above the transitional support, we already have the permanent GST Voucher (GSTV) scheme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It defrays GST for lower- to middle-income Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When the GST is raised, I will enhance the permanent GSTV scheme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will maintain the Government’s public commitment to (a) fully offset the GST for the lower half of retiree households; (b) significantly offset the GST for the upper half of retiree households; and (c) offset about half of the GST for lower-income households with no elderly persons.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is the Government’s way of ensuring our system of taxes and transfers remains progressive and supports Singaporeans through the change, while enabling us to fund our future needs in a sustainable way.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even as we navigate our near-term challenges, we must maintain our focus on the longer term, and on Singapore’s future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have spoken about the accelerating structural shifts in the world in my previous Budget speeches: first, the decline in support for globalisation; second, the shift in global economic weight towards Asia, which brings new opportunities; third, the rapid advancement of technology, and more recently, the risk of a technologically bifurcated world; and finally, our own transition to an ageing society, which presents challenges and opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must understand these shifts and their deep implications as we chart our future together as one Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: After the Second World War, nations experienced several decades of growth and prosperity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Trade barriers fell, and global trade grew rapidly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Prosperity gave governments the resources to establish comprehensive safety nets and welfare programmes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These included unemployment benefits, pensions and healthcare, among others.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But at the same time, globalisation and technology created winners and losers, and widened income inequalities between the skilled and unskilled.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There are growing sentiments that globalisation and the multilateral system have failed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: An ageing population, disruption to jobs and slowing economic growth are adding to fiscal pressures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Yet, it is politically untenable to cut back on social benefits.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When governments issue debt to fund social spending, they impose a growing debt burden on the next generation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is happening at a time when the global economy is experiencing weaker growth and dampened sentiment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Central banks have lowered interest rates to unprecedented levels.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition, asset purchases by central banks have resulted in abundant liquidity and raised concerns over the formation of asset bubbles.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In fact, with limited fiscal space and ultra-low or even negative interest rates, governments and central banks are much less able to mount stabilisation measures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On the strategic front, the friction in the United States (US)-China relationship is a major source of tension and uncertainty, affecting global economic growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The recent Phase 1 trade deal between them has headed off an immediate escalation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But it will not resolve the underlying strategic competition.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This involves political systems, ideologies and values, and goes beyond trade and technology.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On present trends, US-China tensions will recreate geopolitical fault lines and portend a bifurcated global order.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have sketched out the global structural shifts, economic uncertainties and strategic tensions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I trust Members will see that we are entering a very challenging time.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But we can, and we will, pull through.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To deal with these major shifts, we need a capable government, working closely with our people and a good plan.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a city-state, we are small, but nimble.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are a trusted node for trade and investment between Asia and the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is because of our political stability, commitment to rule of law and multilateralism, ease of doing business and strong intellectual property (IP) protection regime, among others.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a multicultural society, we have welcomed diversity and embraced openness.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our diversity has made us stronger and more valuable to the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have come together and weathered many past storms, like the Global Financial Crisis, the severe acute respiratory syndrome (SARS), and now, the ongoing COVID-19 outbreak.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Budget 2020 is our strategic financial plan to prepare Singapore and Singaporeans to meet these challenges and seize new opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This Budget, I will lay out our plans in four areas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, to grow our economy, transform our enterprises, to create opportunities for our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, to care for and nurture Singaporeans at every stage of their lives, to build a caring and inclusive society, where no one is left behind.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, to build a liveable and sustainable Singapore in the face of climate change, secure our sovereignty as an independent nation and ensure our fiscal sustainability.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And fourth, to mobilise Singaporeans to work together in this journey to build a nation and a home we will always call our own.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The structural changes I described earlier bring both opportunities and challenges.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Technology and innovation will drive our productivity and our next phase of growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Amidst declining support for globalisation, most of Asia remains committed to free trade and economic integration.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Asian economies have strong growth drivers and are projected to account for half of global GDP by 2040.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore is well-positioned to make the most of these structural changes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is an improvement over the 2.2% per year growth in the preceding three-year period.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our enterprises are entering new markets and doing business globally.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Singapore Business Federation’s 2019 National Business Survey shows that eight in 10 enterprises have an overseas presence, up from seven in 10 the previous year, despite global uncertainties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Their spirit of enterprise augurs well for the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Overall, these efforts at enterprise transformation have translated into good wage growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Two years ago, I set out our vision of Singapore as a Global-Asia node of technology, innovation and enterprise.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our economy will be one driven by innovation and digitalisation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore will serve as a launch pad for multinationals and regional corporates to access Asia, and for Asian enterprises to go global.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our enterprises will compete on value and reach new customers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And these enterprises will be powered by a skilled, adaptable and Asia-ready workforce.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To support this vision, in this Budget, I will introduce a set of measures to drive our Transformation and Growth strategy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There are three key thrusts: first, enabling stronger partnerships; second, deepening enterprise capabilities; and third, developing our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a small, open economy, we must continue to strengthen partnerships with the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have an extensive network of economic linkages, including Free Trade Agreements (FTAs), International Investment Agreements and Avoidance of Double Taxation Agreements.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, Minister Indranee Rajah signed our latest Avoidance of Double Taxation Agreement with Indonesia earlier this month.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond economic connectivity, we are enhancing our digital connectivity to create new value.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore Customs is connecting our Networked Trade Platform with the customs portals of our trading partners.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It will foster interoperability, and address frontier issues like artificial intelligence (AI) governance, to enable more trade.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The digitalisation of finance will also open up new ways of doing business.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Players from different domains and around the region are coming together to bid for the Monetary Authority of Singapore's (MAS') digital banking licences.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To make the most of our global links, we must strengthen partnerships within Singapore to bring good ideas to global markets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Under our Research, Innovation and Enterprise 2020 Plan, we are sustaining investment into promising ideas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These include AI, industrial robotics, urban solutions and sustainability, and the biomedical sciences, among others.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Through partnerships among the Government, industry and the research community, we are turning these ideas into new businesses with global potential.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For instance, Singapore was one of the first cities to allow autonomous vehicle (AV) testing on public roads.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many AV players have set up here, testing their technologies with the National University of Singapore (NUS) and Nanyang Technological University (NTU), seeking to win the global race.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the biomedical industry, the number of startups has doubled from 2014.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: More than 300 biomedical startups are now bringing discoveries from bench to bedside and looking to export them to the region.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In fact, our research institutes are part of the global fight against COVID-19, developing diagnostic kits already in use here and sent to China.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is one of the fruits of our long-term investments in research and innovation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Within each industry, we need to strengthen partnerships to deepen industry-wide capabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even as our enterprises compete to differentiate themselves, they must come together to solve common challenges.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Trade Associations and Chambers (TACs) play an important role.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, the Container Depot and Logistics Association (Singapore) is developing an electronic payment system that can help depot operators and transport companies save time and cost.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To sustain the good progress, we will enhance our support for TACs to scale up and raise the capabilities of their industries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I have covered how we are deepening partnerships.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The second thrust of our Transformation and Growth is to deepen capabilities at every stage of an enterprise's growth, from starting up, to growing, to transforming further.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our enterprises must be the incubators of innovation, the crucibles for skills upgrading and the creators of good jobs for our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many of our enterprises are deepening their capabilities by innovating, digitalising and venturing overseas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These include smaller companies like Yong Leng Trading Company, a local provider of sealing solutions for industrial customers, and PDS International, a developer and distributor of personal protective equipment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By adopting digital platforms, they have accessed new markets, raised revenues and reduced costs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Goldbell Group, an industrial vehicle leasing company, launched an inhouse accelerator, while Moveon, an optics manufacturer, partnered our research institutes to develop enhanced production technologies for micro-optical systems.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will enhance our support to enterprises, at each stage of their growth, to deepen their capabilities in an enterprise-centric way.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There are about 3,800 technology startups in Singapore and about 150 venture capital funds investing in startups here and in the region.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our startup ecosystem is ranked in the top 15 globally in the Global Startup Ecosystem report.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Startup SG helps startups get their ideas off the ground.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It provides holistic support, including co-investments, mentorship and physical space.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Through co-investment schemes like Startup SG Equity, we have catalysed over $560 million in private sector funding over the last four years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This year, we will improve support for deep-tech startups.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Deep-tech startups are those in emerging technology areas, such as pharmbio and medtech, advanced manufacturing and agri-food tech.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They have high potential to be competitive and stimulate innovation in their sectors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But these startups need larger investments, longer gestation periods and face higher risks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Investors are, hence, less prepared to invest in deep-tech startups.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will give deep-tech startups better access to capital, expertise and industry networks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond startups, many enterprises, both new and established, are seeking to grow.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This Package aims to help enterprises identify business needs, adopt pre-approved digital technologies and take the first steps to enter new markets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, we will launch the GoBusiness platform, a single touchpoint for enterprises to transact with the Government digitally.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, we will drive greater adoption of digital technology.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will expand the SMEs Go Digital programme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Across all 23 ITM sectors, we will have Industry Digital Plans or equivalents, and enable enterprises to access pre-approved digital solutions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, to help more enterprises enter new markets, we will enhance the Market Readiness Assistance grant by expanding the funding support and coverage, to include, for example, FTA consultancy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must continue to support the growth of our enterprises and, as they mature, drive deeper transformation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, through the Enterprise Development Grant (EDG), Enterprise Singapore provides integrated support for enterprises to innovate and internationalise.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For enterprises to transform, they need to strengthen their leadership and management capabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This year, we will introduce an Enterprise Transform Package, with a focus on leadership.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Enterprise Singapore will launch the Enterprise Leadership for Transformation Programme to support business leaders of promising SMEs in achieving the next bound of growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the next three years, we aim to support business leaders of 900 enterprises in business transformation, with training and mentorship.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will work with institutes of higher learning (IHLs), banks and industry experts and facilitate collaboration.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In tandem, we will continue to broaden transformation through EDG by expanding its reach.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The third thrust of our Transformation and Growth effort is to develop our people, so as to enable our people to access good jobs, earn good wages and stay employable.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Economic growth is a means to creating a better life for our people.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must nurture every Singaporean to their fullest potential.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government's promise to Singaporeans is this: regardless of your starting point, as long as you are willing to learn, we will support you to learn throughout life – in pre-employment, in your working years and as we pursue lifelong learning and employability.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will bring in different partners, including IHLs, enterprises and the Labour Movement to help you do so.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our IHLs provide a strong foundation in learning and have partnerships with industry.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: IHLs and the industry have distinct roles, and by aligning these to keep learning relevant, students can secure good jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Employment rates are high and starting salaries have increased.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We develop Singaporean talent in partnership with enterprises under the Singapore-Industry Scholarship scheme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many of them have graduated and are developing their careers with leading enterprises like ST Engineering and Micron.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our local students are well-prepared to thrive in other countries and cultures, including in Asia.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: About half of all local IHL students today gain experience abroad through programmes, such as internships, exchanges and service learning or study trips.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In my pre-Budget dialogue with youth leaders, I was struck by their understanding of the importance of learning new skills and exploring new opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They look forward to overseas exposure and postings in the region.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Beyond pre-employment education, we must also support our people who are already at work.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With shorter technology cycles and more intense global competition, skills acquired when we are young need to be constantly refreshed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Career transitions will be more common, even the norm.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our SkillsFuture movement seeks to enable our people to learn, develop new skills and stay employable.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Five years after the launch of SkillsFuture, we have made good progress.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This includes Mr Koh Wui-Tek, a FinTech executive who applied his learning in project management to serving his clients, as well as Mdm Juriah Jahaya, a certified trainer, who deepened her people development skills.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singaporeans are also upskilling and accessing good jobs in growth sectors with the support of employers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Younger Singaporeans are undergoing on-the-job training while getting a qualification.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singaporeans who have been working for some time have adapted and grown their skills.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One good example is Ms Nur Hidayah Binte Abu Bakar, whom I met at Workforce Singapore (WSG) last year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: After leaving the electronics industry, Ms Hidayah joined AETOS Holdings as an Auxiliary Police Officer.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: She went through the tough training as part of the Professional Conversion Programme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, she not only earns more and has a clearer career pathway, but she is also helping to keep Singapore safe.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am very encouraged by the efforts made by Singaporeans to acquire new skills in the midst of the major structural changes in the global economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To further support them in this journey, the Government will invest in the Next Bound of SkillsFuture.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There will be three elements to this: first, enabling the individual; second, enhancing the role of our enterprises; and third, a special focus on mid-career workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The top-up will be available for use from 1 October 2020.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Unlike the earlier $500 credit which had no expiry date, this top-up will expire in about five years, by end-2025.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is to encourage Singaporeans to take action early to learn new skills and to make the best use of this period of economic slowdown.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, we want to enhance the role of enterprises in developing their staff.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Enterprises know best the skills needed for their business to transform, and can play a key role in helping their workers learn and apply new skills.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By investing in their staff, they build a stronger workforce, which can, in turn, help enterprises succeed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, we must strive to achieve this virtuous cycle.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A good example is Containers Printers, a local food packaging company.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It has adopted digital technology and trained its workers to take on higher value-added roles like real-time monitoring of production.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In our unique tripartite model, the Labour Movement plays a crucial role.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We cannot keep jobs, enterprises or even industries that are no longer viable.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Instead, we refresh, retrain and rejuvenate for the long term.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, the United Workers of Electronics and Electrical Industries and Thales, a French technology leader, have set up a Company Training Committee.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Management staff and union members are working together to develop training plans and deepen skills, so that workers can take on better jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On my visit to Thales, I was very heartened to hear how its employees are upskilling and contributing to Thales’ transformation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a good example of how unions and enterprises can work together to keep workers up to date as enterprises transform.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Employers can use this enterprise credit to defray 90% of out-of-pocket costs of business transformation, job redesign and skills training.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, we will also provide more support for job redesign.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Third, we will work with large anchor enterprises to support training for their sectors and value chain partners.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our aim is to make this a mainstream pathway, with 12% of each cohort going through these pathways, up from 3.5% today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Fifth, as more enterprises train their workers, we will deepen workplace learning capabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Ministry of Education (MOE) launched the National Centre of Excellence for Workplace Learning (NACE) at Nanyang Polytechnic in July 2018.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: MOE will expand NACE to two more IHLs over the next few years and aim to benefit over 1,200 enterprises, especially our SMEs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In line with our focus on the role of industry in SkillsFuture, we will also recalibrate Government funding towards training providers and courses with a stronger link to job and wage outcomes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The third element in the Next Bound of SkillsFuture is a special focus on mid-career workers currently in their 40s and 50s.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Born in the 1960s and 1970s, they grew up in a time when our economy was just starting to take off.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When they started work, it was normal, even celebrated, to stay with one job, in one company, for life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As enterprises restructure, the nature of jobs has changed.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many have adapted to these changes, picked up new skills, and even switched careers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ms Ng Lee Chun, 50, is one of them.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: After leaving her previous job, WSG helped her to secure a logistics role with ST Logistics.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Through the Professional Conversion Programme for Supply Chain Professionals, ST Logistics sent her for training for this role.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some workers in their 40s and 50s have not seen any job or career changes since leaving school or had the chance to upskill earlier.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But they are now facing greater competition from younger workers and workers overseas.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the same time, with broader global shifts, exciting jobs will emerge.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our mid-career workers can seize these opportunities and do better for themselves and their families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We aim to double the annual job placement of locals in their 40s and 50s to around 5,500 by the year 2025.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To reach this goal, we will increase the capacity of reskilling programmes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These will include the Professional Conversion Programme under the Adapt and Grow initiative, career transition programmes delivered by Continuing Education and Training (CET) centres, like IHLs, and sector-specific programmes like the TechSkills Accelerator Company-Led Training for information and communications technology jobs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In tandem, our employers must step up to recruit, retain and retrain our local mid-career workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will provide a hiring incentive to employers who hire local jobseekers aged 40 and above through a reskilling programme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For each eligible worker, the Government will provide 20% salary support to the employer for six months, capped at $6,000 in total.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In parallel, we will streamline our manpower schemes, including support for hiring and retention, to maximise their impact.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To improve access to reskilling programmes, I will also provide a special SkillsFuture Credit top-up of $500 to every Singaporean aged 40 to 60 in 2020.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will be over and above the top-up that I announced earlier.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This additional credit can be used for selected reskilling programmes at CET centres.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Like the broad-based top-up, this additional credit will expire in about five years, to encourage early action.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Apart from Government support, we will assemble a group of volunteer Career Advisors from professional communities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These advisors will provide peer-level support and career guidance to local workers in navigating professional pathways.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We hope that all these initiatives will provide meaningful support to those in their 40s and 50s to further their careers with confidence.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Lifelong learning and contribution does not stop at the 40s and 50s.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As our people live longer, we will provide more support to help them remain active and contribute to our society and economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many seniors have told us that they want to continue working and learning.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Besides saving more for retirement, it is about a sense of agency and purpose, and staying active and connected.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government has strongly supported enterprises that employ our seniors through the Special Employment Credit (SEC), the Additional SEC (ASEC) and WorkPro.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For our seniors who wish to work longer, earn more and save more, the Prime Minister had announced at last year’s National Day Rally that we are raising the Retirement and Re-employment Ages.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are also increasing the Central Provident Fund (CPF) contribution rates for workers aged 55 to 70.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Like SEC and ASEC, this Senior Employment Credit will provide employers with wage offsets when they hire Singaporean workers aged 55 and above, with the support levels tapering down over time as the Retirement and Re-employment Ages are gradually raised.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In short, even as we support workers' aspirations to work longer, we hear employers' concerns.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As part of our unique tripartite system, the Government has stepped up to support both our workers and our enterprises.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even for seniors who choose to retire, but wish to continue to learn and stay active, the $500 SkillsFuture Credit top-up that I just announced will support this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Retirees can use this to deepen their interests, or even to explore a whole new area, be it cooking or coding.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For many years now, foreign workers have been part of our workforce.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With our declining local labour force growth, foreign workers are a necessary complement.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But we must regulate the inflow carefully in a way that creates opportunities for our locals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One area of particular concern is S Passes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These are skilled jobs, many of which can be done by locals, such as polytechnic diploma holders.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We created the S Pass category because despite our best efforts, we are not producing enough of such skilled locals.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: S Passes enable enterprises to top up their workforce with more skilled workers and to recruit workers with particular skills that locals may lack.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But S Passes should not be a means by which enterprises hire low‑cost foreign workers when qualified locals are available.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last year, we announced cuts for the Dependency Ratio Ceiling (DRC) and S Pass sub-DRC thresholds for the Services sector.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This was to manage manpower growth and encourage our enterprises to restructure and reskill our local workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have been monitoring the manpower growth closely.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The number of S Pass holders in the Construction, Manufacturing, Marine Shipyard, and Process sectors is growing by 3.8% per year over the last two years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The number could increase significantly over the next few years, as the Construction and Marine Shipyard sectors recover and the Process sector begins work on projects in the pipeline.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, the growth in S Pass holders must be sustainable.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government has been working closely with industry and educational institutions to build up a pipeline of local manpower, including mid-career workers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We want them to have fair opportunities to grow, while supporting the manpower needs of enterprises.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will phase in the cuts in two steps.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The first step from 20% to 18% on 1 January 2021 and subsequently to 15% on 1 January 2023.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are announcing the changes about a year ahead, to give time for enterprises to adapt.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Given the economic uncertainties, we will not reduce the S Pass sub-DRC for the Manufacturing sector at this point.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But we do want manufacturing companies to make the effort to recruit local skilled workers and technicians, too.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Therefore, when conditions allow, we intend to tighten the S Pass sub-DRC for Manufacturing, too.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the same time, we recognise the potential concerns of enterprises about the availability of skilled manpower in these sectors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To help you find skilled local graduates looking to embark on their careers and older local professionals looking for new careers, SkillsFuture Singapore (SSG) and WSG will work with you to improve matching.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Enterprises that have specific needs can continue to apply for additional manpower flexibilities in exceptional cases, through schemes, such as the Lean Enterprise Development Scheme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In view of the economic conditions, I will maintain the foreign worker levy rates for all sectors for 2020.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the immediate term, we are facing headwinds with the shocks and uncertainties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But in the medium term, we are facing deep structural shifts in the global economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will support our enterprises and workers with the near-term challenges, through the Stabilisation and Support Package for workers and enterprises.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To tackle medium-term challenges, our Transformation and Growth strategy will support efforts to deepen enterprise capabilities, develop our people and forge stronger partnerships, through our tripartite structure.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By positioning Singapore as a Global-Asia node of technology, innovation and enterprise, we can ride on the next wave of structural changes resolutely.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The respective Ministers will provide more details of the schemes I have mentioned in this section later.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It also gives us the resources to support our people with their needs, to build a caring and inclusive home.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our tax and spending policies reflect our values.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the past decade, we have significantly increased our social spending.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last year, we gave out about $1.1 billion in cash to Singaporeans who need more help.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The payouts were provided through structural schemes, such as ComCare, for the vulnerable, Workfare Income Supplement for lower-wage workers, GSTV – Cash for lower-income Singaporeans and Silver Support for the vulnerable elderly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This social spending reflects our commitment to invest in our people, to give every citizen a stake in our society, to care for our seniors and to provide more help to those with less.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This Budget, we will continue to care for Singaporeans in the following ways: first, we will build on our efforts to support our families; second, we will support and enable our seniors in their retirement years; and third, we will promote a stronger giving culture.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will, first, touch on how we will further support our families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Good education provides a strong foundation for children to grow, realise their aspirations and continue a journey of lifelong learning.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have committed to decisive shifts in the Government’s support for early childhood development.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are determined to give every child, regardless of circumstances, a good start in life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As the Prime Minister announced at the National Day Rally last year, we will step up efforts to improve the affordability, accessibility and quality of preschool services.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Overall, we are doubling our support for our young in their preschool years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 2018, the Government spent about $1 billion on the early childhood sector.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the primary to pre-university school years, education is already heavily subsidised for Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Primary school is free for all Singaporeans, while the secondary school fee is $5 a month.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Students pay only a few dollars of miscellaneous fees.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For students from lower-income families, we will provide further help.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will enhance the MOE Financial Assistance Scheme by raising the annual bursary quantum for pre-university students, from $900 to $1,000.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also increase transport subsidies for all students and school meal subsidies for secondary school students.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The enhanced Financial Assistance Scheme will cost an additional $9 million per year, or a total of $52 million per year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We announced that we would enhance bursaries for diploma and degree holders last year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These bursaries are on top of subsidies that are provided to all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Starting from Academic Year 2020, students from lower- and middle-income families in the polytechnics and autonomous universities can benefit from higher bursaries.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also enhance bursaries for full-time Institute of Technical Education students from Academic Year 2020.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Students from households which qualify under the lowest-income tier for the bursaries will now receive 100% fee subsidy on top of the cash bursary.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Students from low- and middle-income households will also benefit from an increase in the cash bursary quantum by up to $200 a year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A good education lays a strong foundation for a better future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is why this Government has been providing significant education subsidies for each child.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A Singaporean child will receive over $180,000 of education subsidies in total by the time he turns 16.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This includes about $50,000 in Government subsidies over five years when they enrol in a full-day childcare programme with one of the Anchor Operators.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For those who come from less-privileged backgrounds, there are additional subsidies for preschool, bursaries and other financial assistance schemes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This substantial investment is how we maximise every child's potential, regardless of family circumstances.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a promise that I, as a former Education Minister and now Finance Minister, am committed to keep.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When Singaporeans are ready to start a family and own a home, we make sure that there is good access to quality and affordable housing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last year, the Ministry of National Development consolidated existing housing grants into the Enhanced CPF Housing Grant.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We expect around 16,000 HDB households to benefit from these enhancements each year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government has made significant moves to help Singaporeans manage major expenditures in life, through structural subsidies in education, healthcare and housing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This year, with the economic slowdown and the uncertainties of the COVID-19 outbreak, we are mindful that many families are facing greater pressures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: During my fellow Members of Parliament and my own walkabouts, people often tell us that they are worried about job security and rising expenditures.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will help to free up cash for other household expenses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In addition, I will extend the Service and Conservancy Charges Rebate by another year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Eligible HDB households will receive rebates of between one-and-a-half and three-and-a-half months.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Lower-income Singaporeans will get additional help with their daily living expenses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In October 2019, we announced the Workfare Transport Concession Scheme and the Public Transport Voucher to help cushion the transport fare increases for lower-income households.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singaporeans on Workfare will receive 20% more for work done in 2019, with a minimum payment of $100.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will also help needy Singaporeans more directly.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They will receive Grocery Vouchers worth $100 each year in 2020 and 2021, for use at major supermarkets.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This directly helps needy households with one of their major cost of living items – food.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There will be additional help for families taking care of children and elderly parents.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will provide a further $100 cash payout for every adult Singaporean with at least one Singaporean child aged 20 and below this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will provide an additional GST Voucher – U‑Save rebate for larger households with five or more members, to help them with their utilities bills.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Together with the U-Save Special Payment I mentioned earlier, larger households can receive a total of 2.5 times their regular U-Save rebates this year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These households can receive up to $1,000 in U-Save rebates, depending on their flat type.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will also provide a $100 top-up to the PAssion Card to all Singaporeans aged 50 and above this year, including the Pioneer Generation and Merdeka Generation seniors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This can be used to pay for groceries, activities and facilities at Community Clubs and more.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Those who do not currently have a PAssion Card can get one for free to receive the top-up.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our Self-Help Groups have also been working closely with the community to help needy families and children.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To enable them to do more, I will provide a $10 million grant to them over two years so that they can help more families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Community Development Councils (CDCs) have also played an important role in partnering the community to strengthen bonds and help vulnerable groups.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Each CDC has its set of local assistance schemes to meet local needs and programmes that allow community members to help those with extra needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will provide $20 million for the CDCs to do more and better meet the needs of their residents through local initiatives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Together, the Care and Support Package will provide a young family with about $1,300.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A 3-Generation family can receive more – about $1,800.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: More details are provided in the slide and in the Annex.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our life expectancy at birth is close to 85 years, the longest in the world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore will not just be a great place to raise a family, but a great place for seniors to live a life of purpose, dignity and contribution.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Community Networks for Seniors is now a national programme, with 650 active ageing nodes to engage our seniors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must see ageing as a positive force and turn this phase of life into a time of opportunity.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ageing with confidence includes having financial assurance in retirement.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This can be achieved through a combination of individual effort, family, community and Government support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the years, we have strengthened the four pillars of our social security system of home ownership, CPF, healthcare assurance and income from Workfare and Silver Support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have also been enhancing the ComCare schemes, which support Singaporeans who are unable to work and have little or no family support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: CPF is a major scheme to enable Singaporeans to save enough for their retirement years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We need to keep on updating and improving our CPF policies over time so that they remain appropriate for each cohort.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
