text: We have been adjusting the Basic Retirement Sum (BRS) regularly, in line with rising income levels.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Since 2017, household incomes per capita have risen by an average of 4.1% per year in nominal terms, while BRS has increased by 3% per year.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to adjust BRS by the same 3% per year for the next two cohorts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These modest continuing adjustments are necessary for the payouts to keep up with basic retirement expenses.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With continuing wage growth, each successive cohort has been able to save more.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We expect seven in 10 actively employed persons from these two cohorts to be able to set aside their BRS, significantly more than four in 10 about a decade ago.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Even as more seniors are prepared for retirement, one group of current seniors may not be able to meet their retirement needs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When they were younger, they earned less than working Singaporeans do today, even after adjusting for inflation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some may have earned lower wages for most of their working lives.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Others may have stopped working early to take care of family members.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are in a fortunate position that most of our seniors have housing assets that they can use to support their retirement, if they wish.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will do more to help Singaporeans tap their housing assets for retirement by enhancing the Silver Housing Bonus and the Lease Buyback Scheme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for National Development will provide more details.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: CPF is a good retirement scheme, based on personal savings.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It provides Singaporeans with very favourable risk-free interest rates on their savings.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many Singaporeans want to top up their own, their spouse’s or parents’ CPF accounts.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 2019, such voluntary cash top-ups added up to about $1 billion.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We would like to encourage more to do so, particularly those whose CPF balances are on the low side.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Lower- to middle-income Singaporeans aged 55 to 70 who have not been able to set aside the prevailing BRS will be eligible.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a way of encouraging and augmenting family support for our seniors with fewer means in retirement.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While CPF is a good scheme, for a small segment of the elderly population, it will not be enough.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some had low incomes during their working years and currently have little or no family support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We created the Silver Support Scheme to complement the CPF for this group and give them more financial security in retirement.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The scheme is now almost five years old and a review is timely.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For individuals living in smaller flats, this means that the cash payouts will increase from $750 to $900 per quarter.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will also broaden the eligibility criteria of Silver Support.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will expand the threshold for lifetime wages and per capita household income to cover more seniors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There will also be a new payout tier to provide a smaller payout to seniors whose monthly household incomes per person are above $1,300 but not exceeding $1,800.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These seniors do not receive Silver Support today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Eligible seniors will be notified by CPF Board and start receiving payouts under the enhanced scheme from December 2020.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The cost of Silver Support will nearly double, from today’s $330 million, to around $620 million in 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Here is an illustration of how the matched savings, right-sizing and enhanced Silver Support can add up to help a retired 65-year-old couple to more than double their retirement income.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will pause here for Members to take a look at the example and details are in the Annex.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These enhancements underscore the Government’s commitment to provide seniors with greater assurance in retirement and reflect the values we hold dear, such as taking care of our parents and seniors.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They will also complement the other schemes for our seniors, such as the Pioneer Generation Package and Merdeka Generation Package.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also help seniors stay active and contribute to the community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many senior volunteers find that volunteering gives them purpose, keeps them socially connected and promotes active ageing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The community also benefits from their wealth of experience and skills.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There is Mr Victor Lim, a 70-year-old retiree who spent 40 years in the Medical Imaging and information technology industry and now volunteers at the Infocomm Media Development Authority's Digital Readiness programmes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There is also Mdm Leong Su Yin, one of the oldest members of Retired Senior Volunteer Programme (RSVP), who has been volunteering for over 20 years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our success in taking care of every Singaporean, from preschool to retirement, is only possible with the support of our community partners.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This brings me to the third strategy – Strengthening the Giving Culture.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When we harness and rally greater participation and resources from the community, we can better support those in need.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will continue to support the community in building a stronger giving culture.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Last year, I announced the Bicentennial Community Fund, which provides dollar-for-dollar matching for donations made to Institutions of a Public Character (IPCs).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is on top of the 250% tax deduction provided for donations made to IPCs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One of the potential beneficiaries is the Daughters Of Tomorrow Limited, which helps disadvantaged women gain new skills and find employment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will provide a pool of funds that our Social Service Agencies (SSAs) can tap on to transform themselves for the future.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I hope they will make good use of this to strengthen their organisational capabilities, become more productive and enhance their service infrastructure, in partnership with MSF and NCSS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Just like how our efforts in the ITMs have positioned our enterprises and economy for the future, the Community Capability Trust will equip SSAs to bring the social sector forward.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There is much value to be gained when a community comes together in support of a cause.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These are ground-up initiatives that support inclusion and celebrate the abilities of persons with special needs through activities like music and sports.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Everyone can play a part to build an inclusive society from their hearts in ways big and small.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many enterprises have also built inclusive workspaces for persons with disabilities (PwDs).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To support the employment of PwDs, the Special Employment Credit (SEC) and the Additional Special Employment Credit (ASEC) schemes provide wage offsets for employers hiring Singaporean PwDs earning below $4,000 a month.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the last Budget, we extended the SEC and ASEC until the end of 2020.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have received good feedback on the schemes in supporting PwD employment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To ensure that the EEC remains helpful for PwDs to find employment and remain in the workforce, the Government will review the EEC after two years and make adjustments if necessary.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These funds provide a safety net for the low-income by helping them to meet their daily expenses and healthcare fees.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The respective Ministers will provide more details of the schemes I have mentioned in this section later.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will continue to support our families through the enhancements to our education and housing schemes, and the Care and Support Package for households.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will enable our seniors by promoting active ageing and providing financial assurance in their retirement years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also partner the community to build a stronger giving culture so that we can better support those in need.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is our continued effort to improve the lives of our people and our future generations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must continue to work together to build a society where opportunities are available to every Singaporean, at every stage of life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our Pioneers set out to build a high-quality living environment, even when they had to attend to pressing economic and security challenges.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They left us a legacy of a clean, green and liveable environment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The generation that planted the seeds does not fully benefit from their toil, but they care to do this for future generations to reap the fruits.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the same spirit, we must plant the seeds to secure a better future for generations to come.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: By thinking long term, by confronting major challenges and by investing for our future, we have beaten the odds.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Three major challenges we must continue to confront are: climate change, security and fiscal sustainability.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To build a liveable and sustainable home, we must address climate change.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a low-lying island nation, rising sea levels threaten our very existence.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, what can we do as a small island nation?

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, we must continue to support global efforts to combat global problems.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore must continue to do our part as a responsible member of the international community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singapore plays an active role at the United Nations Framework Convention on Climate Change.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Besides representing our interests, Team Singapore is regarded as an honest broker, helping to build bridges and consensus.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This year, we will update our commitment to the Paris Agreement and take a further step to chart our vision for a low-carbon, sustainable future Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister in the Prime Minister’s Office will elaborate on this later.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, we must manage our transition to a low-carbon, low-emissions economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must turn our carbon constraints into a strength, just like how we have turned our water vulnerabilities into an area of strength with radical innovations in NEWater and desalination.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, Singapore is a global hub of water research and innovation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The circular economy – turning waste into a resource that can be reused in the production cycle – is one way we can reduce our carbon footprint and open up new opportunities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: NEA will soon begin a field trial to use NEWSand, made from incineration ash, in road construction along Tanah Merah Coast Road.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The research will focus on renewable energy, cooling Singapore and carbon capture, among others.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As climate change is global, innovative solutions created here can be commercialised, turning our constraints into a strength.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: More broadly, we have to manage our greenhouse gas emissions, by putting in place the right incentives, tax structures and regulations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We introduced a carbon tax in 2019 and supported enterprises in improving energy efficiency.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We introduced and enhanced the Minimum Energy Performance Standards to raise the energy efficiency of energy-intensive household and industrial appliances.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The domestic transport sector contributes a significant amount of greenhouse gas emissions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Vehicles with internal combustion engines (ICEs) also contribute to pollution, adversely affecting our health and quality of life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many major cities have already set ambitious goals to phase out ICE vehicles and shift to cleaner technologies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Car manufacturers are actively developing cleaner engine technologies, such as hybrids and electric vehicles (EVs), and are exploring new areas, such as hydrogen fuel cells.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a small city-state, we are able and have a strong reason to stay abreast of these major technological changes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For both public health and climate change reasons, we should progressively phase out the use of ICE vehicles towards cleaner alternatives, such as hybrids and EVs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will set a long-term strategic goal for Singapore to achieve this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To promote this, we will have three measures in this Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: First, we will enhance incentives to encourage the adoption of cleaner and more environmentally friendly vehicles.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In 2018, we introduced the Vehicular Emissions Scheme for cars and taxis.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Under the scheme, car buyers and taxi operators who choose cleaner car models can receive an upfront rebate of up to $20,000 and $30,000 respectively.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have seen promising results from the scheme.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: More car buyers and taxi operators are choosing environmentally friendly engines, such as electric hybrids.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Therefore, we will introduce a similar scheme called the Commercial Vehicle Emissions Scheme for light goods vehicles.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources will announce the details at the Committee of Supply (COS).

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will also revise the road tax methodology for cars to better reflect the current trends in vehicle efficiency from January 2021.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This will lead to an across-the-board reduction in road tax for EVs and some hybrids.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Second, we will expand the public charging infrastructure for EVs.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, there are about 1,600 charging points island-wide.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will work with the private sector to step up the deployment of chargers in public car parks.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will progressively procure and use cleaner vehicles to do our part for the environment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Here, we are placing a significant bet on EVs and leaning policy in that direction because it is the most promising technology.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It also requires a significant increase in demand to justify the infrastructure investment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a significant undertaking involving multiple agencies.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The transition towards EVs will have a major impact on tax revenues.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Fuel excise duties today yield around $1 billion per year and are significant contributors to Government revenues.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: They are also a form of mileage tax, which discourages excessive driving, especially in private cars, and thus helps to reduce road congestion.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But EVs do not pay fuel excise duties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Therefore, we will need to update our vehicular tax structure to preserve these two considerations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ideally, we would like to implement a usage-based tax on EVs as an alternative to fuel excise duties.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But the technology to do this properly on EVs is the Next Generation Electronic Road Pricing (ERP) System, and distance‑based charging using ERP is still several years away.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Total road tax, after the revision in methodology and the new lump-sum tax, will be higher for some EV models.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, EV buyers can expect to enjoy substantial cost savings because of the significant EV Early Adoption Incentive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I spoke about policy measures that the Government will put in place to reduce emissions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But the Government alone cannot address the threat of climate change.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Therefore, mobilising all of us in this effort is the third thrust of our climate change strategy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Robert Swan, the first person to have walked to the North and South Poles, once said, "The greatest threat to our planet is the belief that someone else will save it." To deal with climate change, we have to foster a climate of change in our community where everyone, whether as an individual, as a business leader or as a community leader, makes conscious decisions to lower our carbon footprint.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One such decision by individuals is our choice of household appliances.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Outside our homes, we earlier announced plans to add more greenery to our HDB estates.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Residents are contributing through the community garden movement.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These gardens keep our shared neighbourhood vibrant and bring people closer together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It will have three key focus areas: reducing energy consumption, recycling rainwater and cooling our HDB towns.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I spoke about how we are committing to global efforts, managing our carbon constraints and building a sustainable Singapore, together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must try hard and we will do our part.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But the course of climate change depends on the commitment of all nations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The risk of rising sea levels remains significant.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, our fourth strategic thrust is to prepare our island for rising sea levels.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Minister for the Environment and Water Resources will elaborate on our immediate plans at the COS.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Prime Minister mentioned at the National Day Rally last year that climate change adaptation might cost $100 billion or more over 100 years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is a major fiscal outlay in the coming years.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I will top it up subsequently whenever our fiscal situation allows.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must have the resolve to deal head-on with the existential threat of rising sea levels.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Just as our Pioneers planted the trees for us to enjoy today, we must protect our island for future generations to come.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our food security may also come under threat, as imported supplies come under strain from climate change or geopolitical tensions.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: To improve our food resilience, the Minister for the Environment and Water Resources will provide more details of our "Grow Local" strategy at the COS to pursue our "30/30" aspirations.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In uncertain times, there are many calls on our Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, we cannot take our peace, prosperity and stability for granted.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As a small city-state, we are particularly vulnerable to volatilities in our external environment.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Securing our home remains a high priority in our Budget and must be funded adequately.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is imperative that we continue to invest in our external, internal, cyber and data security, to keep Singapore and our families safe and secure.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Diplomacy and deterrence are the twin pillars of maintaining Singapore's sovereignty.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We strive to build good relations with our neighbours and international partners and to promote a rules-based world order.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: A strong Singapore Armed Forces supports our diplomatic efforts and ensures that other countries take Singapore seriously.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must be ever-ready to defend our interests should negotiations fail.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must continue to draw a credible deterrence, by maintaining our military and technological edge, in a prudent manner that stretches every defence dollar.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Back home, we are committed to protecting our safety and our way of life.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our Home Team agencies will continue to enhance the operational readiness of their officers, leverage technology and build partnerships with the community.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Singaporeans share a strong conviction to look out for one another and to partner the Home Team to prevent and deal with terror threats and crises, through the SGSecure movement.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must also be prepared to deal with cyber threats, as digitalisation becomes more pervasive.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our cyber capabilities have been raised significantly, with the setting up of the Cyber Security Agency (CSA) in 2015 and the passing of the Cybersecurity Act in 2018.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: CSA is preparing measures for the next level of cybersecurity, as we adopt more advanced technologies, such as AI, Cloud and the Internet of Things.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: All of us, in the Government, enterprises and as individuals, will need to stay vigilant and strengthen our cyber and data security capabilities.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Data security is also a vital prerequisite and key enabler of Singapore's Digital Economy.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is key to preserving trust in a digitally-connected world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We enacted the Personal Data Protection Act in 2012 and the Public Service has adopted comprehensive measures to secure and protect citizens’ data.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The respective Ministers will provide more details of the schemes to confront the challenges of climate change and security.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As we lay out our plans for our economy, people and environment, we must ensure these plans are fiscally sustainable, so that we have the resources to deal with future needs and challenges.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must continue to plan our finances based on long-term structural drivers.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We can end up having more, or less.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But we must not count on such revenue surprises to keep happening.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must anticipate long-term spending needs and be disciplined to raise revenues ahead of time, so that we can continue to provide quality public services to all Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: At the same time, we must be mindful of the uncertainties and downside risks to our revenue.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: There are ongoing discussions to revise international tax rules under the Base Erosion and Profit Shifting project and we are actively participating in them.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Major long-term infrastructure is lumpy and requires hefty upfront investments.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: But once built, they benefit many generations of Singaporeans.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Borrowing for such developments allows us to distribute the cost equitably across current and future generations, without the need for sharp increases in taxes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: However, we must remain disciplined about our use of borrowing.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We should continue to pay for recurrent needs, like healthcare expenditure, through recurrent revenues, such as taxes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This, in turn, lowers the borrowing costs of enterprises and households, and promotes a virtuous cycle of economic growth.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must also maintain our fiscal posture and leave enough to deal with unexpected shocks and longer-term challenges.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Constitution requires us to run a balanced budget over each term of Government.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We are being prudent to preserve fiscal buffers, to ensure that we have the wherewithal to stand our ground and bounce back quickly if the tide turns against us.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is how we have been able to respond decisively to fight the COVID-19 outbreak and support Singaporeans and our workers and, at the same time, to be able to set aside an Assurance Package for GST to help Singaporeans in the years ahead.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The accumulated surpluses at the end of the term of Government becomes part of our Past Reserves, which are invested.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Today, the Net Investment Returns Contribution (NIRC) from our Reserves is the biggest component of our revenue.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is remarkable for a country with no natural resources of any kind.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am making further changes to our tax system to strengthen its resilience while maintaining competitiveness.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is due mainly to lower-than-expected expenditures arising from unforeseen project delays.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: When we exclude the Government’s top-ups to funds and NIRC from our Reserves, we expect a basic deficit of $5.1 billion, or 1% of GDP.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This, together with the Stabilisation and Support Package, will impart a considerable fiscal boost to the economy to address near-term concerns.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: On the whole, we expect an overall deficit of $10.9 billion or 2.1% of GDP.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: With our fiscal prudence since the beginning of this term of Government, we have sufficient accumulated fiscal surplus to fund the overall deficit in FY2020.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Members have been very patient and this is my third file.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is almost two hours now, so, thank you very much.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Before I start on the third file, some good news.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: My very dedicated staff in MOF who worked day and night with me over the weekends and Chinese New Year, managed to trim and trim the speech and grow and grow the substance.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: So, the substance has grown, but, the speech is more concise now.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We have moved all the details to the Annexes.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It is a pity because there were so many inspiring stories that I wanted to share with Members, but I hope that they will find many opportunities to share these stories.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We can succeed only if we work together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our ongoing fight against the COVID-19 outbreak is a testament to how we can work together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Our healthcare workers and frontline officers are giving their all to keep us safe, and care for those who are unwell.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: And others, such as our community groups, enterprises and many volunteers, have stepped forward.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Everyone has something to offer and every action makes a difference.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: This is the spirit of the Singapore Together movement which I launched last June – to build a democracy of deeds, mobilise the creative energies and commitment of Singaporeans, find common cause and beat the odds together, to build our future Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We made a concerted effort to involve Singaporeans and stakeholders in our strategic deliberations and budgeting process.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Over the course of the Budget 2020 consultations, my colleagues and I met almost 1,000 leaders from different parts of society, including our unions, enterprises, social sector and youths.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: It was a very enriching experience for everyone and I thank every participant.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Some of you will recognise your ideas in the Budget.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, we enhanced the internationalisation support schemes after receiving feedback from TACs, such as the Singapore Manufacturing Federation and the Association of Banks in Singapore.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We provided more resources to support our people to take action to reduce carbon footprint, after several youth leaders I met suggested this.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I also thank the talented students from Nanyang Polytechnic for the artistic illustrations in my slides today.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Many Singaporeans are coming up with, and acting on, ideas to make Singapore a better place.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: In the area of climate change, youths like Ms Cheryl Lee and her team in the Singapore Youth for Climate Action have been organising activities to encourage youths to take action through simple lifestyle choices.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Ms Rohini d/o Ravindran is also contributing to the community, by conducting photography and videography sessions for lower-income youths to develop their problem-solving skills and build a good foundation for them to excel.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: One example is Progress NEST started by Mr Akram Hanif to support children from low-income families.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Through these partnerships, we have been able to do more and do better.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government is committed to expanding and scaling up successful ground-up projects, such as those supported by OSF.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Channelling the energies of our people to key causes requires us to identify the challenges of our time.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These challenges are multifaceted and multidimensional, but they are ultimately about how Singapore remains exceptional in an increasingly complex world.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The solutions will also come in all shapes and forms, from all levels of society – from Government policies to individual efforts on the ground.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We must overcome these challenges and find solutions together.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The Government will work with agencies and key stakeholders to identify major societal challenges.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: For example, our AI Healthcare Grand Challenge is drawing strong interest here and with partners from France and Germany.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: Under the National Innovation Challenge in Ageing, we sought ideas to combine different technologies to enable ageing in place and deployed these solutions at a precinct level.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: While we are only in our initial phases, we have learnt useful lessons and seen encouraging results.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: We will issue more specific challenges to encourage ground-up participation.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: These include challenges in the social sector, where we have built many community partnerships to better support children from low-income and vulnerable families, and promote youth mental well-being, amongst other things.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: The respective Ministers will provide more details of the schemes I have mentioned in this section later.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: I am excited about the prospect of stronger Government-citizen partnerships in overcoming these challenges and look forward to the results that these partnerships will yield.

speaker: The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance (Mr Heng Swee Keat)
text: As this Budget has many measures, MOF has prepared a booklet summarising the measures, which I hope colleagues will find useful.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: (In Mandarin):   	The COVID-19 outbreak has brought about many uncertainties globally.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The virus disregards nationalities and the effort to control the disease is a global one.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Governments, international organisations, researchers and healthcare workers from many countries are now working closely together.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: China has taken a series of highly effective measures and an early success of China in fighting COVID-19 will help both China and the world.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The current situation has brought about widespread impact to our economy.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Some sectors have already been affected, and Singaporeans are worried about their employment prospects.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Singapore has enough resources to meet present challenges.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This is because we have been well-prepared accumulating surpluses from this term of Government, in order to meet unexpected expenditures.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Whether we can successfully overcome this challenge will depend on whether Singaporeans can look out for one another and maintain social cohesion.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: When facing the unknown, it is natural that people feel worried.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We should pay attention to personal hygiene and be considerate towards people around us.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: At the same time, we must take concrete actions to help those who are in need.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Budget is a long-term strategic plan to ensure that Singapore develops sustainably and Singaporeans can lead better lives.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In overcoming our short-term challenges, we must also pay attention to the long-term structural changes and capture the opportunities brought about by these changes.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: First, we must continue to encourage enterprises to transform and create more opportunities for Singaporeans.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As the saying goes, “there is no end to learning”.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: However, in order to meet increasing recurrent expenditures, such as in healthcare, the GST increase will still be needed by 2025.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Third, we must continue to develop Singapore, look after Singapore's security and stability, and ensure that we have a sustainable fiscal system.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This is our commitment to our future generations.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Fourth, we will work together with Singaporeans to build a nation and home we will always call our own.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: As the saying goes, "the young will be educated, those in need will receive support, the old will be cared for", we hope that Singapore will not only be a good place for raising children, but also a place where our seniors have dignified and meaningful lives.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will enhance our current Silver Support Scheme to help lower-income seniors cope with daily expenses, providing them assurance in their retirement.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In addition, we will introduce the Matched Retirement Savings Scheme to help those who do not have very high CPF balances build up their CPF savings.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We also encourage our senior citizens to lead active and fulfilling lives after retirement.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: At present, the global situation is uncertain and many countries face structural changes.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Taking a long-term point of view, dealing with this sudden virus outbreak is only one of the challenges that we will encounter as we go forward.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Together, we have to march towards our common objective.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In the spirit of the Singapore Together movement, as long as we pool our efforts and work hand in hand, we will be able to solve all problems and create an even better Singapore.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: (In English): I will now conclude in English.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: All nations, big or small, will have to devise strategies and mobilise their people to navigate these changes and turbulence.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Singaporeans have enjoyed more than half a century of stability and prosperity because we have seized the opportunities from an increasingly open and interconnected world.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Every decade or so, when a test comes, we have rallied and passed it together.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: In this Budget, I have outlined our plans not only to help our people deal with near‑term challenges, but also to better enable Singaporeans of all ages to thrive in the new decade.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Stabilisation and Support Package, costing $4 billion, will help viable enterprises and our workers during these uncertain times.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: Our Transformation and Growth effort, costing $8.3 billion over three years, will support our longer-term plans to position Singapore as a Global-Asia node of technology, innovation and enterprise.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: The Care and Support Package, costing $1.6 billion, will support our households and alleviate concerns over cost of living.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: This is on top of the structural social subsidies given to Singaporeans in healthcare, education and housing.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: We will continue to take steps towards climate change mitigation and adaptation, to ensure that in the decades ahead, our children and children’s children will have a safe and liveable Singapore.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: I am confident that, together, we can ensure that Singapore remains exceptional.

speaker: Mr Heng Swee Keat
text: And as one Singapore, we will work together with fellow Singaporeans, to build a nation and a home we will always call our own.
